treatment.earlyblight: Early Blight • Common fungal disease caused by fungus. Appears as dark spots on older leaves. Apply copper-based fungicides. Remove infected fruits. Improve air circulation.
treatment.powderymildew: Powdery Mildew • White fungal coating on leaves and stems. Apply copper-based fungicides. Remove infected leaves. Ensure proper spacing for airflow.
treatment.lateblight: Late Blight • Serious fungal disease causing rapid crop failure. Apply systemic fungicides immediately. Remove all infected plants. Destroy crop residues.
treatment.leafspot: Leaf Spot • Various fungal diseases affecting leaf tissue. Apply fungicides. Remove lower infected leaves. Mulch around plants.
treatment.leafmold: Leaf Mold • Fungal disease causing yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces. Improve ventilation. Apply fungicides. Remove infected leaves.
treatment.anthracnose: Anthracnose • Fungal disease causing dark, sunken lesions. Apply copper-based fungicides. Remove infected fruits. Improve air circulation.
treatment.bacterialspot: Bacterial Spot • Bacterial infection causing dark spots. Use copper-based bactericides. Remove infected plants. Practice crop rotation.
treatment.commonrust: Common Rust • Fungal disease with small brown pustules on corn leaves. Apply fungicides containing azoxystrobin or propiconazole. Remove severely infected lower leaves. Improve air circulation. Avoid overhead irrigation.
treatment.northernleafblight: Northern Leaf Blight • Fungal disease causing long gray-green to tan lesions on corn. Apply foliar fungicides (e.g. chlorothalonil, pyraclostrobin). Remove crop residue after harvest. Rotate with non-host crops. Plant resistant hybrids.
treatment.healthy: Healthy • No treatment needed. Continue regular care and monitoring.

prevention.earlyblight: Early Blight Prevention • Rotate crops annually to reduce spore buildup. Space plants properly for good air circulation. Avoid overhead watering. Remove lower leaves as plants grow. Use disease-resistant varieties. Scout regularly for early signs.
prevention.powderymildew: Powdery Mildew Prevention • Maintain proper plant spacing for ventilation. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Monitor humidity levels. Use resistant varieties. Apply preventive sulfur spray. Keep plants healthy and stress-free.
prevention.lateblight: Late Blight Prevention • Use certified disease-free seed potatoes. Plant resistant varieties. Practice long crop rotation (3-4 years). Avoid overhead irrigation. Destroy volunteer plants. Monitor weather conditions closely.
prevention.leafspot: Leaf Spot Prevention • Improve air circulation between plants. Avoid wetting foliage when watering. Use drip irrigation instead of overhead. Remove lower leaves from plants. Rotate crops yearly. Clean pruning tools between cuts.
prevention.leafmold: Leaf Mold Prevention • Ensure adequate greenhouse ventilation. Reduce humidity below 85%. Use disease-resistant varieties. Space plants properly. Water at soil level. Remove lower infected leaves promptly.
prevention.anthracnose: Anthracnose Prevention • Use certified disease-free seeds and plants. Practice crop rotation with different crop families. Avoid overhead watering and working in wet foliage. Remove infected fruit immediately. Mulch to prevent soil splash.
prevention.bacterialspot: Bacterial Spot Prevention • Use disease-free seeds and transplants. Practice crop rotation for 2-3 years. Avoid working in fields when plants are wet. Space plants for good air circulation. Remove infected material immediately.
prevention.commonrust: Common Rust Prevention • Plant resistant hybrids. Rotate corn with soybeans or other non-host crops. Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest. Avoid late planting. Scout for pustules from mid-season.
prevention.northernleafblight: Northern Leaf Blight Prevention • Use resistant hybrids. Bury or destroy corn residue after harvest. Rotate with non-host crops (e.g. soybean) for 1–2 years. Avoid planting in low, wet areas.
prevention.healthy: Healthy Crop Prevention • Continue monitoring your field regularly. Maintain proper irrigation and drainage. Ensure balanced fertilization. Scout for early pest and disease signs. Practice good farm hygiene.
